# Disagreement Log — Didache Chapter 14

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Didache 14 — Sunday Worship
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 4

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: κυριακὴν δὲ κυρίου — "Lord's Day of the Lord" vs. "Lord's Day"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "the Lord's day of the Lord" |
| LOGOS | "the Lord's Day" |
| PNEUMA | "the Lord's Day" |

**Issue:** The Greek combines the adjective κυριακήν (Lord's) with the genitive κυρίου (of the Lord) — an unusual redundancy that may be emphatic. EMET's literal rendering is awkward.
**Ruling:** "The Lord's Day" adopted (LOGOS/PNEUMA). The emphatic redundancy noted in translator commentary.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.1: θυσία — "sacrifice" vs. "offering"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "sacrifice" |
| LOGOS | "sacrifice" |
| PNEUMA | "sacrifice" |

**Issue:** Unanimous agreement. θυσία is the standard sacrificial term; all agents correctly render it "sacrifice." This is historically significant and should not be softened.
**Ruling:** "Sacrifice" unanimous.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.2: "dispute" vs. "quarrel" — framing the prerequisite

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "dispute with his fellow" |
| LOGOS | "dispute with a fellow believer" |
| PNEUMA | "unresolved quarrel with another person in the community" |

**Issue:** ἀμφιβολία = dispute/quarrel (lit. something thrown both ways). "Dispute" and "quarrel" both work; LOGOS adds "fellow believer" to specify the community relationship.
**Ruling:** "Dispute with a fellow believer" (LOGOS) adopted. The community context is important.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.3: θαυμαστόν — "wonderful" vs. "marvellous"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "wonderful" |
| LOGOS | "marvellous" |
| PNEUMA | "wonderful" |

**Issue:** θαυμαστόν = wonderful/marvellous/astonishing. Both English words are accurate; "wonderful" has deeper usage in English Bible translations of Mal 1:14.
**Ruling:** "Wonderful" adopted (EMET/PNEUMA). Matches standard English rendering of Malachi.
